symbols.name: prime modulus base
symbols.meaning: A fixed prime; on this page it is not a sequence length.
symbols.quote: Fix a prime $q$ (on this page $q$ is a prime, not a sequence length), and let $b\ge1$ be the number of base-$q$ digits of a field.

symbols.name: field digit count
symbols.meaning: The number of base-$q$ digits of a field.
symbols.quote: Fix a prime $q$ (on this page $q$ is a prime, not a sequence length), and let $b\ge1$ be the number of base-$q$ digits of a field.

symbols.name: field value count
symbols.meaning: The number of values a field can take, q^b.
symbols.quote: Put $Q=q^b$, the number of values a field can take, and let $V$ be the array volume, the number of stored data bits.

symbols.name: offset
symbols.meaning: The offset in [Q] added to the target field, prepared from the control values.
symbols.quote: where $a\in[Q]$ is the offset, prepared from the control values.

symbols.name: suffix bit count
symbols.meaning: The number of bits following the target field.
symbols.quote: If $B$ bits follow the target, the target and its suffix form $Q$ consecutive blocks of $B$ bits.

symbols.name: scaling integer
symbols.meaning: A fixed positive integer prime to q by which the target field is multiplied; not the machine constant.
symbols.quote: Let $c$ be a fixed positive integer prime to $q$ (not the machine constant).

symbols.name: wrap count
symbols.meaning: The integer part of cy/Q, counting how often cy wraps past Q.
symbols.quote: The map $y\mapsto cy \pmod Q$ sends the block at position $y$ to position $y'=cy-jQ$, where $j=\lfloor cy/Q\rfloor$ counts how often $cy$ wraps past $Q$.

symbols.name: new position
symbols.meaning: The position cy-jQ to which the block at position y is sent.
symbols.quote: The map $y\mapsto cy \pmod Q$ sends the block at position $y$ to position $y'=cy-jQ$, where $j=\lfloor cy/Q\rfloor$ counts how often $cy$ wraps past $Q$.

symbols.name: unit denominator
symbols.meaning: The positive integer prime to q in the denominator of a rational unit c/c'.
symbols.quote: A rational unit is a signed ratio $c/c'$ of positive integers $c,c'$ both prime to $q$.
